newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes firm in quiet Asia, wet market moves little.
newsitem.headline: Crudes firm in quiet Asia, wet market moves little.

text.p: Crude oil prices were mostly indicated firmer in Asia on Monday, while the wet market was generally quiet as most January barrels appeared to have been placed, traders said.
One trader said cold weather worries in the northern hemisphere were supporting the futures market, and that this was serving to offset news that Iraq might shortly resume limited crude oil exports.
January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $22.85/22.90, compared with the IPE settlement of $22.77 on Friday.
The paper market was mostly steady.
January Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $1.70/1.75, while February Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $1.75/1.80 after a recent deal was done at $1.81 between a trader and a major.
In the wet market, January Oman was notionally assessed at MPM plus 15 to 20 cents, although most traders said they believe virtually all January barrels have been placed.

Masila appears to be about the only Gulf crude still actively discussed in the market, traders said. The crude was assessed fetching a price of about Dubai plus $1.10-$1.20, after a deal was believed done at a premium of $1.05 or $1.10.
The January Masila deal was believed done last week.
In Asian crudes, December and January Tapis were assessed fetching a premium of $1.00 above published quotes.
ADNOC said it has cut the price of its crudes lifted in November by between 70 to 75 cents per barrel.
Murban, Lower Zakum and Umm Shaif were all reduced by 70 cents a barrel to $23.10, $23.15 and $22.85 respectively. Upper Zakum was cut by 75 cents a barrel to $21.20.
The price of China's Daqing crude oil for November lifting to Japanese customers has been calculated at $22.05, down 56 cents from October.--M.Yoshikawa/Tokyo (+81-3-5473-3706)
